description: MEWS is Sandia National Laboratories' Python package for altering building-weather files with extreme events and local climate adjustments. It produces multiple weather scenarios for probabilistic studies, not simulating weather physics. Inputs are historical or projected EPW weather records and event assumptions; outputs are modified weather files for building-energy tools. It currently implements extreme temperatures, while the README describes hurricane work as preliminary. Geographic coverage, event duration and temporal resolution follow the supplied weather file. The own LICENSE.md calls the package Revised BSD, with separate licences for dependencies, so the source is free. A limitation is that DOE-2 weather handling has not been tested since the first version; the repository calls its docs incomplete and identifies the current example. MEWS can supply heat-stress inputs to building and infrastructure resilience simulations. An altered EPW file should not be treated as an observed event. No weather files were obtained or generated here.
name: MEWS extreme-weather file generator
